title: Dreyer et al. 2023 — A large EEG database with users' profile information for motor imagery brain-computer interface research
description: A large EEG database from 87 healthy participants recorded during a single-day motor imagery brain-computer interface (BCI) experiment, organized into three datasets (A, B, C) that share the same protocol. Participants imagined left- and right-hand movements in a Graz protocol with calibration and online training runs (240 trials per participant). The database also includes demographics, personality profiles, and cognitive traits, so it can be used to study how user profiles relate to BCI performance and to develop cross-user classification algorithms.
methods_description: EEG was recorded at 512 Hz with a g.USBAmp (g.tec) and active electrodes: 27 EEG channels plus EMG and EOG, referenced to the left earlobe with ground at FPz. Each participant completed 6 runs of 40 trials, 2 calibration runs with sham feedback and 4 online training runs with real feedback. Each trial lasted 8 s, with a red arrow cue followed by continuous visual feedback. Online processing used participant-specific frequency band selection (5-35 Hz), a fifth-order Butterworth filter, CSP spatial filtering and an LDA classifier. Participants also completed questionnaires on demographics, personality (16PF5), cognitive traits, spatial abilities and learning style.
